newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers warn Netanyahu against war.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers warn Netanyahu against war.

text.p: Thirty-three Israeli reserve soldiers have written to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warning him against bringing war on the Jewish state, Israeli television and Israel Radio said on Saturday.

"The fighting spirit and the readiness to sacrifice are conditioned on the knowledge that the government is doing all it can in order to prevent war," an excerpt of the letter broadcast on Channel Two television said.
"In light of recent developments, we have been cut off from that fighting spirit, without which we do not see how we can take part in the next war," the letter added.
Last month 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in fierce clashes and gun battles spurred by Israel opening a second entrance to a tourist tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem.

Jordan's King Hussein, who signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1994, has been outspokenly critical of Netanyahu since the clashes erupted. Egypt, the first Arab state to make peace with Israel, in 1979, and Israel have been waging a war of words.
Syria has yet to resume peace negotiations with Israel since Netanyahu took office in June. An official Syrian newspaper on Saturday accused Netanyahu of trying to start war in the Middle East.

Netanyahu, who ousted Israel's previous centre-left government in May elections, opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace with Arab states and the Palestinians. The principle was key to nearly five years of peace talks conducted by the previous government.
